new_entry.model_policy: A selected recording branch, not a universal national sound or a claim that every release uses this ensemble. Published credits establish the sound-producing instruments; exact materials, models, techniques, room, signal chain, tuning approximation and numeric axes are authored representative defaults unless expressly sourced. Photos identify relevant musicians and do not claim to document the modeled recording session. Original existing recipe optimization is retained: these source defaults do not promise verbatim preservation in every compressed output format.

tradition.name: Finnish modern jazz
tradition.lineage: Contemporary Finland-connected improvised music, represented by Verneri Pohjola’s Bullhorn quartet. Trumpet, piano, acoustic bass and drums balance memorable compositions, lyrical lines and bursts of rougher energy.

extras.description: An authored quartet gives a clear trumpet theme room to expand into more urgent passages. Piano voicings, mobile bass and responsive kit playing support changing intensity rather than a fixed atmospheric wash. The album’s guest saxophone, trombone and cello are optional colors and are not stacked into the four-player default. Exact instrument makes and materials are author-selected.

new_entry.geo_rationale: The releasing label identifies Pohjola as Helsinki-based and credits album mixing there. This is the selected modern-scene anchor, not a claim that every performance was recorded in Helsinki.

sources.title: Bullhorn, Edition Records credits and artist statement
sources.support_notes: Explicit core quartet: Pohjola trumpet, Aki Rissanen piano, Antti Lötjönen bass, Teppo Mäkynen drums. Guest personnel separately listed. Artist describes intimate improvisation and rough energy;2014 recording/mixing locations documented.

new_entry.neighbor_distinction: Modern scene subset illustrated by a trumpet-led compositional quartet. It differs from the Finnish jazz solo-piano branch selected elsewhere and avoids treating Nordic origin as a requirement for low energy or ambient spaciousness.
